criteria.notes: The workspace provides the requested full PDF surface: multiple documents, navigation, search, outlines, forms, annotations, zoom, download, commands, lazy rendering, and unattended scrolling.
No external design reference was declared; the controlled-document workspace brief is the visual authority.
A restrained records-workspace shell frames real document pages without copying the card or dashboard grammar of other examples.
Workspace controls retain their declared signage text floors; PDF page readability remains explicitly user-controlled through fit and zoom.
Dark, light, and custom toolbar/sidebar palettes preserve control contrast while keeping document paper neutral.
Document names, status labels, tabs, and controls remain bounded without clipped glyphs across all inspected surfaces.
Full HD, portrait, compact, square, landscape, and wide-low surfaces retain usable navigation and a bounded document viewport.
Both PDFs, annotation icons, PDF.js runtime, worker, editor assets, and all palette states load without broken requests.
The example is a document tool rather than a dashboard template and exists to teach opt-in rendering mechanics.

screenshots.notes: Full-HD reader, sidebar, document surface, and bottom controls were inspected at rendered size.
Compact mode removes the sidebar and retains an unclipped page and complete navigation.
Landscape preserves the full workspace shell with a centered, correctly fitted page.
Portrait light mode keeps the sidebar usable and renders consecutive pages at readable width.
Automatic scrolling advances through fully painted pages without black or blank render churn.
Declared compact mode matches the inspected sidebar-free reader and bounded toolbar.
Declared Full-HD state exposes both documents, form actions, and a complete page.
Declared portrait state retains complete navigation, document continuity, and light-theme contrast.
Single-page custom-theme mode keeps outline navigation, one complete page, and bounded controls.
Square mode uses its constrained viewport without overlap; fit and zoom remain available.
Wide-low mode preserves all workspace actions and a complete fit-page view without clipping.
